title: Ion chemistry to form the buidling blocks of aromatic chemistry in space
description:
A major limitation of current astrochemical models and chemical reaction networks is the lack of isomer-specific kinetic data and structural identification of reaction products. Experimental constraints on chemical networks are often difficult to obtain because the most thermodynamically stable isomer is not necessarily the most chemically reactive one. Reactive isomers are frequently produced in low abundances, rapidly isomerize into more stable structures, or are challenging to isolate under laboratory conditions. Consequently, their intrinsic reactivity and associated rate coefficients remain poorly characterized. As a result, many reactions are either omitted from astrochemical networks or represented by isomer-averaged rate constants, introducing substantial uncertainties into model predictions.

You will take part in the development of an instrument that combines ion mobility and mass spectrometry with laser spectroscopy in order to address the critical challenges aforementioned.
